Article Title: Sadhguru pledges Rs 1 crore for Nepal flood relief, seeks joint Himalayan response
Article Text:
Sadhguru called for a collective approach to managing disasters and protecting the Himalayan ecosystem

Sadhguru calls for Himalayan Board

Sadhguru Jagadish Vasudev has pledged Rs 1 crore towards Nepal’s Prime Minister Disaster Relief Fund to support rescue and relief efforts following devastating flash floods along the Nepal-Tibet border. He also called for greater cooperation among Himalayan nations, proposing a five-nation Himalayan Board to coordinate responses to disasters affecting the fragile mountain region.Sadhguru made the remarks on Sunday while addressing an event titled “In Solidarity With Nepal” in Kathmandu, his first public appearance since the disaster. According to an official statement by the Isha Foundation, the event brought together people in Kathmandu to express solidarity with those affected.The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) said the death toll from the flash floods has risen to 903, while thousands remain missing.Among those still unaccounted for are 77 participants of the Isha Sacred Walks Kailash Sojourn. The group was at the Gyirong immigration centre on the China side of the border when the disaster struck. Three Isha volunteers stationed on the Nepal side are also missing, according to the foundation.The Isha Foundation, founded by Sadhguru, organises Kailash Mansarovar pilgrimages each season. Pilgrims travel from Kathmandu through Nepal to Tibet, with trekking on foot forming part of the journey.Alongside his financial support for Nepal’s relief efforts, Sadhguru called for a collective approach to managing disasters and protecting the Himalayan ecosystem. He proposed a five-nation Himalayan Board comprising India, China, Pakistan, Nepal and Bhutan.Arguing that the Himalayan mountain system cuts across political boundaries, Sadhguru said countries sharing the range needed to coordinate their actions."The mountains don't know your political affiliation. The mountains don't know what nonsense or language you speak. Even if you cannot administer it as one body, at least consultation must happen as one body. There must be some congruence of action in what we do because the Himalayas are the most fantastic and majestic feature on the planet. At the same time, they are very fragile," Sadhguru asserted.He called for the proposed body to be established urgently, saying the Himalayas needed to be treated as a shared natural system rather than as separate national concerns."A body comprising all these nations where the Himalayan ranges run has to happen now. Even if political administrations are separate, the mountain ranges have to be looked at as a feature that needs to be protected for future generations on the planet.If we don't do this and go on thinking, okay, it's Nepal's problem, let them deal with their problem, there will never be a solution."Sadhguru also said the scale of the disaster was beyond what could reasonably have been anticipated and argued that Nepal could not be expected to deal with its aftermath alone."Nobody expected something like this to happen, that three-fourths of a glacial ice cube will just fall down four thousand feet down the peak. Not something anybody calculates it for. But now that it's happened, we must look at this because this is not something a small nation like Nepal can solve by themselves," Sadhguru said.
Article Summary: Sadhguru Jagadish Vasudev has pledged Rs 1 crore towards Nepal’s Prime Minister Disaster Relief Fund. He also called for greater cooperation among Himalayan nations, proposing a five-nation Himalayan Board to coordinate responses to disasters affecting the fragile mountain region.

Article Title: CJP netas not saints ... nothing wrong in having political ambitions: Wangchuk
Article Text:
Sonam Wangchuk says CJP organisers may have political ambitions, but that's acceptable if platform remains non-party.

NEW DELHI: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk has said Abhijit Dipke and his fellow organisers of the Cockroach Janta Party movement appear to have political ambitions, but there is nothing objectionable in this as long as the student platform retains its non-party character.Wangchuk, in a Prakhar Gupta Xperience podcast, said Dipke and the others had not disclosed any plans to him and his view was based on his own assessment. “Political ambition is very normal,” he said. “Past political connections I don’t care about, present and future political aspirations are not a problem.”“They are not such saints that they want absolutely nothing and are doing all this entirely selflessly,” he said, referring to the possibility that the organisers had personal or political aspirations.Assessing their suitability for leadership, Wangchuk described the organisers as “well meaning”, “quite skilled” and “above average”.“Well meaning but unskilled” could create difficulties, while “very skilled but ill meaning” would pose a much greater danger, he said.Asked whether they could become corrupt, Wangchuk said he had seen no such indications. “People go through changes, and I hope they won’t,” he said.Wangchuk said the organisers could join an existing party or launch a new one later, but must not turn the CJP platform into their political vehicle. He said he had advised them to preserve it as a “neutral, apolitical pressure group”, arguing that this would help retain the trust of supporters who saw it as a students’ movement rather than an organisation aligned with BJP, Congress or AAP.Wangchuk acknowledged that his own standards sometimes led him to expect public figures to have no political ambition. That, he said, could be unrealistic because the organisers were ordinary people entitled to pursue political careers. Beginning such a career by championing an education-related cause could, in fact, be positive.He also expressed hope that participation in the movement would help them emerge as more mature and grounded politicians. “I am actually happy about that,” Wangchuk said of their taking up public issues.
Article Summary: Sonam Wangchuk says CJP organisers may have political ambitions, but that's acceptable if platform remains non-party. Wangchuk said the organisers could join an existing party or launch a new one later, but must not turn the CJP platform into their political vehicle.

Article Title: Punjabi influencer Manjeet Kaur, who died after being 'tied to a tree, burnt alive', was 7 weeks pregnant: Autopsy
Article Text:
Manjeet Kaur (Image Credit: Instagram)

CHANDIGARH: Social media influencer Manjeet Kaur, 28, was nearly seven weeks pregnant when she died in hospital after allegedly being abducted from Chandigarh and set on fire in Morinda, according to her autopsy report.Kaur died during treatment at the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER) in Chandigarh on August 26, nearly two months after she suffered severe burn injuries.Also read: ‘Why was her statement not recorded': 6 mysterious questions in influencer's death Police are now trying to trace and arrest two suspects, identified in the FIR as Shubhi and Pinda. They have been booked for kidnapping and murder following a complaint by Kaur’s mother, Kanta Devi.According to the complaint, Shubhi and Pinda, who were acquaintances of Kaur, called her to Sector 34 in Chandigarh on the intervening night of July 3 and 4.They allegedly assaulted her, forced her into a vehicle and took her to a forested area near Morinda, where she was allegedly tied to a tree and set on fire.Another acquaintance who reached the spot later managed to put out the flames using a blanket, police said.Kaur was initially taken to a hospital in Morinda before being shifted to Max Hospital in Mohali. She was later admitted to PGIMER, where she remained under treatment until her death.Also read: Who was Manjeet Kaur? Inside the life of Punjabi influencer who died after being 'set on fire' The case has also raised questions over an alleged delay in recording Kaur’s statement.Sources said Kaur regained consciousness during her treatment and sought to have her statement recorded. The PGIMER police post reportedly informed Kharar Sadar police that she was conscious and in a condition to give a statement.The information was also conveyed to the investigating officer, but he allegedly did not reach the hospital, sources said.A daily diary report (DDR) was reportedly recorded at the PGIMER police post regarding the communication.After Kaur died on August 26, the PGIMER police post again informed Kharar Sadar police. The investigating officer subsequently reached the hospital.Kaur’s mother was later taken to the Sector 34 police station, where her statement was recorded and an FIR was registered on Wednesday night.Police are now investigating the circumstances surrounding Kaur’s alleged abduction and death, as well as the events leading up to the attack.
Article Summary: Social media influencer Manjeet Kaur, 28, was nearly seven weeks pregnant when she died in hospital. She died during treatment at the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER) in Chandigarh on August 26. Police are now trying to trace and arrest two suspects, identified in the FIR as Shubhi and Pinda. They have been booked for kidnapping and murder.

Article Title: Ahead of SCO, Uzbekistan joins India in condemning cross-border terrorism
Article Text:

As the 2 countries elevated their relationship, Uzbekistan joined India in unequivocally condemning terrorism, including cross-border terrorism, in all its forms and manifestations, reiterated zero tolerance approach to terrorism and rejected justification of terrorism on any ground whatsoever in a joint statement.Even though the 2 countries share strong counter-terrorism cooperation, this formulation is significant as Uzbekistan has not used the specific phrase "cross-border terrorism" in the past apex-level joint statements (between PM and president), like those issued after summit meetings in 2015, 2018 and in 2020. According to official sources, this reflects stronger diplomatic alignment on state-sponsored terrorism and regional security dynamics, especially in the context of the SCO summit on Tuesday in which leaders will address issues like the need for stronger counter-terrorism and the Afghanistan situation."Leaders called for concerted actions against terrorist entities and for disrupting terrorism financing networks, safe havens and infrastructure. Leaders stressed that those responsible for terrorism should be held accountable and their perpetrators, their backers, facilitators and affiliates should be brought to justice," said the joint statement.The strongest wording so far had come in the 2020 joint statement, after a virtual summit, in which PM Narendra Modi and President Shavkat Mirziyoyev strongly condemned terrorism in all its forms and manifestations and also underlined the need for every country to ensure that its territory is not used to launch terrorist attacks against other countries.Read more: India, Uzbekistan target long-term uranium pact On this occasion, the leaders stressed the importance of strengthening cooperation in law enforcement, intelligence-sharing, and combating violent extremism, and illicit drug trafficking, organized crime, and cyber threats. They also reaffirmed the importance of continued cooperation under the Joint Working Group on Counter Terrorism in the joint statement.India and Uzbekistan, which shares border with Afghanistan, have shared concerns about radicalisation and influx of militant groups. For India, it's important to work with Uzbekistan and other countries in the region to prevent Afghanistan from turning into a haven for terrorist groups, particularly like LeT and JeM based in Pakistan. Tashkent is also home to Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS), a permanent SCO body responsible for coordinating efforts by member-states against terrorism, extremism and separatism."The Leaders reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening cooperation within the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), recognizing it as an important platform for enhancing mutual trust, promoting regional peace, security and stability, and expanding cooperation in trade and economic affairs, investment, and cultural and humanitarian exchanges," said the joint statement.
Article Summary: India and Uzbekistan, which shares border with Afghanistan, have shared concerns about radicalisation and influx of militant groups. For India, it's important to work with Uzbekistan and other countries in the region to prevent Afghanistan from turning into a haven for terrorist groups, particularly like LeT and JeM based in Pakistan.

Article Title: PM Modi likely to hold bilateral talks with Iranian president
Article Text:
PM Modi may hold bilateral meeting with Iranian President Pezeshkian at SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan, their first since the war in the Middle East.

PM Narendra Modi may have a bilateral meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan Monday, official sources said. While Modi landed in Bishkek Sunday, the president was scheduled to arrive Monday morning, according to reports from Tehran.Sources said efforts were on to schedule a meeting between the leaders Monday. This would be the first in-person meeting between Modi and Pezeshkian since the start of the US-Israel war with Iran on Feb 28.The two, in fact, had last met on the margins of the Brics summit in Russia's Kazan in 2024. However, both have spoken with each other on several occasions, including after the West Asia conflict erupted, with Modi stressing the India remains a friend of Iran. Pezeshkian is also likely to visit India for the Brics summit next month.If it happens, the meeting will see Modi reiterate India's position that all issues must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy. He's also expected to highlight India's focus on ensuring the safety and well being of Indian nationals in the region, along with the importance of unhindered transit of energy and goods. The two will also discuss trade, energy and connectivity ties that have come under strain because of the expiry of US sanctions waiver for the Chabahar port.In a difficult balancing act, India has continued to maintain high-level engagement with Iran while repeatedly expressing solidarity with GCC States that came under attack from Tehran for hosting US bases. However, Tehran also expects India to call out the US and Israel for their Feb 28 strikes at the Brics forum, which is currently helmed by India. With the UAE also in the group, the challenge for India would be to forge a consensus on the West Asia situation that would allow a Brics declaration to be issued.
Article Summary: PM Modi may hold bilateral meeting with Iranian President Pezeshkian at SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan, their first since the war in the Middle East. Modi landed in Bishkek Sunday, the president was scheduled to arrive Monday morning, according to reports from Tehran.

Article Title: 'Country Babur came from': Owaisi takes dig at PM Modi's Uzbek honour
Article Text:
Owaisi pointed to Uzbekistan's historical connection with Babur

NEW DELHI: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi took a dig at the BJP after Prime Minister Narendra Modi was conferred Uzbekistan's highest state honour.PM Modi was presented with the Order of "Oliy Darajali Dustlik" by Uzbekistan President Shavkat Mirziyoyev during his two-day state visit to the Central Asian country. The honour is Uzbekistan's highest state award.Reacting to the recognition, Owaisi pointed to Uzbekistan's historical connection with Babur, who he said was born in the Fergana Valley in present-day Uzbekistan and founded the Mughal Empire in India."I congratulate the BJP; the very country from which Babur came to India has conferred an award upon the Prime Minister. The Fergana Valley is in Uzbekistan. Wherever the Prime Minister goes these days, he returns with an award. Congratulations. You used to hurl so many insults in Babur's name, yet the people of that very country are now honoring you with an award. The Sangh needs to reflect on this... We hope that members of the Sangh Parivar and RSS supporters will no longer speak of Babur in that manner," he said.The remarks come against the backdrop of the BJP and RSS's frequent criticism of the Mughal period and references to Babur in political discourse, particularly in discussions around the construction of the Ram temple in Ayodhya and India's history.PM Modi, meanwhile, thanked Mirziyoyev for the honour and described him as his "brother". He said India and Uzbekistan would work together for the welfare of the Global South and humanity."My friend, the father of the economic revolution in Uzbekistan, who has served as a role model across this entire region in scaling new heights of development--this two-day visit of mine will always be remembered," PM Modi said.Owaisi's comments on the award came while he was also criticising RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat over his recent remarks on Hindu-Muslim unity. Bhagwat, speaking at the 'One World One Humanity' event in New York, said there was no difference between human beings and that different religious paths led to the same goal.Owaisi described Bhagwat's remarks as an "old trick from the RSS playbook"."What the current RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat has said is an old trick from the RSS playbook. They will never disavow or retract the things the RSS has consistently stated," he said."There is a distinct difference between the speeches they deliver for the outside world and those meant for their own members--this has always been their playbook style," Owaisi said.
Article Summary: PM Modi was presented with the Order of "Oliy Darajali Dustlik" by Uzbekistan President Shavkat Mirziyoyev during his two-day state visit. Owaisi pointed to Uzbekistan's historical connection with Babur, who he said was born in the Fergana Valley in present-day Uzbekistan.

Article Title: Modi lauds Bengali actor ahead of birth centenary
Article Text:
Modi lauds Bengali actor ahead of birth centenary

Paying tribute to Bengali actor Uttam Kumar ahead of his birth centenary, PM Modi Sunday described him as a versatile actor whose rise despite the failure of several early films offered the lesson to “Never give up”.In his Mann Ki Baat address, Modi said Kumar had become “deeply embedded in people’s hearts” through his acting. Recalling that film lovers believe Satyajit Ray wrote the script of ‘Nayak’ with the “mahanayak” in mind, Modi cited Ray’s assessment that the actor combined “remarkable emotional depth” with dignity. He said Kumar was known for his “natural ease” and philanthropy and “worked very hard” to bring his characters alive.
Article Summary: PM Modi pays tribute to Bengali actor Uttam Kumar ahead of his birth centenary. Kumar had become “deeply embedded in people’s hearts’ through his acting. Kumar was known for his ‘natural ease’ and philanthropy.

Article Title: NEET-PG 2026 smooth; retest for 2.4k Jaipur kids hit by glitch
Article Text:
Over 2.63L appear in NEET-PG; re-test announced for candidates at 2 Jaipur centres

3-member committee to probe power failure

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEET-PG 2026 was conducted across the country on Sunday for nearly 2.7 lakh candidates appearing at 1,111 centres in 339 cities. A retest will be held on Sept 5 for 2,445 candidates at two centres in Jaipur as a glitch disrupted the examination.Dr Abhijat Sheth, president of National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences, said there were no complaints of paper leak, or hacking, and that the examination was conducted in a fair and transparent manner with support from state govts, police, NBEMS experts and faculty members.The NEET-PG 2026 examination was conducted across all 36 states and UTs.The affected candidates were at iON Digital Zone iDZ Sitapura centres, Jaipur, where the examination could not be completed due to an internal power supply problem. Despite repeated efforts, the issue could not be resolved, forcing National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) to postpone the examination for the affected candidates.The health ministry has constituted a three-member committee to probe the power failure at the Jaipur centres. The panel comprises a senior Rajasthan govt official, a joint secretary-level officer from the health ministry and a chief engineer from the Central Electricity Authority.Dr Abhijat Sheth, president of NBEMS said re-examination for the 2,445 candidates will be conducted on Sept 5 at 3pm in Jaipur, with the board assuring that it will be conducted in the same manner and that the candidates' performance would not be adversely affected. "We regret the inconvenience caused to the affected candidates," he said.The nationwide examination was backed by extensive security and real-time monitoring. Around 2,527 faculty members were appointed as independent appraisers, while more than 700 senior faculty members, including deans, directors, medical superintendents and senior professors were deployed as flying squad members.Sixteen NBEMS regional command centres were operational across the country, while examination centres remained under live CCTV surveillance, monitored from the NBEMS headquarters in Dwarka.A dedicated team of 190 NBEMS and TCS personnel monitored the examination in real time. Officials from NBEMS, the health ministry, BEL, ECIL and TCS maintained continuous oversight from the central command centre. Aadhaar-based authentication of candidates was undertaken at examination centres as part of measures to strengthen security and prevent impersonation.
Article Summary: Nearly 2.7 lakh candidates appeared at 1,111 centres in 339 cities. A retest will be held on Sept 5 for 2,445 candidates at two centres in Jaipur. The affected candidates were at iON Digital Zone iDZ Sitapura centres.

Article Title: Right to question not defiance, every dissent not a threat: SC judge
Article Text:
'In a democracy, the right to question is not an act of defiance.': Justice Bhuyan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a constitutional democracy like India, govt must listen to citizens, give space for dissent, and have institutions that are accountable to society and do not treat every dissent as a threat, Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan said on Sunday."In a democracy, the right to question is not an act of defiance. It is an essential expression of citizenship, liberty and constitutional responsibility," Justice Bhuyan said at a convocation ceremony at National Law University, Delhi."If we want a democratic society that respects liberty and difference, that culture has to begin somewhere. It can only begin in our universities. A university... should be one of the first places where the habit of thinking freely begins," he said.A university should be a space where an idea is not accepted merely because it is familiar and where students do not hesitate to ask difficult questions simply because the answer may be uncomfortable,” Justice Bhuyan said.He said India’s Constitution guarantees free speech, thinking and believing differently. “Intolerance begins to undermine that framework when disagreement or dissent is no longer treated as a legitimate difference of opinion but as something that must be silenced, rejected or punished.The ability to live with disagreement is not merely a social virtue. It is the very essence of a liberal constitutional democracy. ”Justice Bhuyan said maturity of a democracy is reflected not merely in how it treated opinions that are popular, having the majoritarian mandate, but also in how it responds to opinions that are difficult, unpopular or inconvenient. “The freedom to express an opinion, to disagree with the prevailing view and to participate in public life would be meaningful only when there is space for dissent,” he added.He quoted Justice O Chinnappa Reddy’s 1986 judgment in Bijoe Emmanuel case, in which the judge had said, “Our tradition teaches tolerance; our philosophy preaches tolerance; our constitution practises tolerance; let us not dilute it.”He pointed out that tolerance under our Constitution does not ask us to surrender our individuality. “It recognises that a free society would contain different opinions, beliefs and ways of looking at the world,” he said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan said in a democracy, the right to question is not an act of defiance. He said India’s Constitution guarantees free speech, thinking and believing differently. “Intolerance begins to undermine that framework when disagreement or dissent is no longer treated as a legitimate difference of opinion," he said.

Article Title: 'Gud khaye, gulgule se parhez': Tejashwi targets BJP-RSS amid Jitan Ram Manjhi-Chirag Paswan reservation spat
Article Text:

Chirag-Manjhi lock horns over quota within quota

NEW DELHI: RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav on Sunday took a jibe at the BJP and RSS , saying, “guḍ khaye, gulgule se parhez”, amid the spat between NDA allies Chirag Paswan and Jitan Ram Manjhi over reservation.The leader of opposition in Bihar assembly also accused the two Union ministers of acting on the “instructions” of the RSS and alleged that the BJP-RSS was “anti-reservation”.He also challenged Chirag and Manjhi to resign from their posts and contest elections from unreserved seats if they opposed reservation.Taking a dig at the two leaders on X, Tejashwi said, “Guḍ khaye, gulgule se parhez!” He alleged that Chirag and Manjhi were speaking in different voices on the issue of sub-categorisation of SC/ST reservations while allegedly acting on the directions of the RSS.“Two Union Ministers, Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi and Chirag Paswan, are speaking in opposite directions on the instructions of RSS, diverting attention from the original objective of BJP-RSS to end reservations, and want to gauge the sentiments of reservation supporters,” he said.He alleged that both ministers, who were elected from reserved constituencies, were benefiting from reservation while being part of the BJP-led NDA.“First and foremost, these ministers, elected from reserved quotas, are sitting in the lap of the Constitution and reservation opponents, enjoying the peak pleasures of power,” Tejashwi said.“If these two have a deep hatred for reservations, let them contest elections from unreserved seats and see their - eyes will open,” he added.Tejashwi also questioned the position of NDA allies in Bihar, including the parties led by Nitish Kumar, Upendra Kushwaha, Chirag Paswan and Jitan Ram Manjhi, on the 65% reservation quota introduced by the state government.“If these parties are pro-reservation, then why don't they get the increased 65% reservation limit in Bihar, raised in our government, included in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution?” he asked.Tejashwi's remarks came a day after differences within the NDA over sub-categorisation of SC/ST reservations became public, with Chirag Paswan and Jitan Ram Manjhi taking opposing positions.The row began after Manjhi and his son, Bihar minister Santosh Kumar Suman, supported the idea of sub-categorisation to ensure that the most deprived Dalit communities receive a greater share of reservation benefits.Chirag, who heads the Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas), strongly opposed any move to review reservation and demanded that Manjhi and his son resign if they supported such a measure.“The constitutional provision of SC/ST reservation is based on social discrimination and not economic status. If they want to change the Constitution, then debate the issue in Parliament. Those who talk or think about reviewing reservation should first resign, as they actually want to completely end it and reduce its scope,” Chirag said.He also asserted that reservation was in place in the past, remains in place today and would continue in the future.Responding to Chirag's demand, Suman said he was ready to resign, but challenged Chirag to take the first step.“As far as resignations go, we are ready. My younger brother’s party is the bigger one; they have more numbers than us and are politically third-generation too, so let them take the lead. Let him step forward by resigning and we are prepared to resign alongside him,” Suman said.Tejashwi also targeted RSS chief over his earlier remarks on reviewing reservation, saying, “Mohan Bhagwat had also spoken earlier about reviewing reservations”, adding that Bihar “ne unke kaan pakad kar achhe se uthak-baithak karwa di thi. Ab phir karenge toh Bihari log RSS/BJP ka murga bana dega.”He was referring to Bhagwat's 2015 call for a review of the reservation policy, which became a major political issue during the Bihar assembly election that year.Tejashwi said ending reservation was “a remote possibility” and accused the BJP of testing public sentiment on the issue. “None can put an end to reservation. RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat called for a review of reservation in 2015, and the people of Bihar taught him a lesson,” the RJD leader said.“These people are merely characters. They only want posts. They are greedy for positions, chairs, bungalows and security, but they have left society behind...” he added.The dispute comes amid renewed political debate over SC/ST sub-categorisation after the Supreme Court's August 1, 2024 Constitution Bench judgment held that states can create sub-categories within SC and ST reservations to ensure benefits reach the most disadvantaged communities.The issue has particular significance in Bihar, where Dalit communities are socially and politically diverse. The state government introduced the Mahadalit category in 2007 to identify the most deprived Dalit communities.
Article Summary: RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav took a jibe at the BJP and RSS, saying, “guḍ khaye, gulgule se parhez”, amid the spat between NDA allies Chirag Paswan and Jitan Ram Manjhi over reservation. He accused the two Union ministers of acting on the “instructions” of RSS.

Article Title: ‘Violation of High Court order won't be tolerated’: Agnimitra Paul reacts after FIR against Mamata Banerjee
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: West Bengal minister Agnimitra Paul on Sunday said that any violation of a Calcutta High Court order, irrespective of the person involved, "would not be tolerated", after an FIR was registered against former chief minister Mamata Banerjee over alleged violations during a Trinamool Chhatra Parishad (TMCP) programme in Kolkata.Speaking to news agency ANI, Paul alleged that the previous Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress government had shown disrespect towards the Calcutta High Court and that judges were repeatedly insulted during its tenure."Any violation of the High Court's order, whether by Mamata Banerjee or anyone else, will not be tolerated. The previous government showed disrespect to the High Court; judges were repeatedly insulted... now, such things will not be tolerated," Paul said.Banerjee and organisers of the West Bengal Trinamool Chhatra Parishad (WBTMCP) programme have been booked by Hastings Police over the alleged violation of a Calcutta High Court order during the organisation's foundation day programme at Cathedral Road on August 28.According to police, the case was registered at Hastings Police Station on August 28 based on a written complaint submitted by Sub-Inspector Apu Baidya.The FIR includes Sections 61(2), 223, 125(a), 132 and 285 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), relating to allegations including criminal conspiracy, disobedience of an order duly promulgated by a public servant, acts endangering life or personal safety, assault or criminal force against public servants, and negligent conduct with respect to public ways.Police alleged that Banerjee and the organisers violated an order passed by the Calcutta High Court in connection with WPA No. 21728 of 2026.According to the complaint, the programme was scheduled to be held from 12 noon to 3 pm under the permission and directions referred to in the complaint. Police alleged that the organisers continued the programme beyond the permitted time.The complaint alleged that Banerjee and the organisers provoked supporters during the programme, following which the crowd pushed aside barricades put up by police.Supporters allegedly jostled with police personnel deployed at the venue, creating a chaotic situation, according to the police account. The gathering also allegedly obstructed vehicular movement on one flank of Cathedral Road.The Calcutta High Court had imposed conditions for the programme, with Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya directing on Tuesday that efforts be made to keep attendance within 1,500.The court had also directed police to ensure that law and order was maintained and that vehicular movement on one flank of the road was not affected.West Bengal minister Indranil Khan also criticised Banerjee, alleging that she had repeatedly disrespected constitutional institutions and the judiciary."Mamata Banerjee never respected the country's laws or its Constitution. Even while serving as Chief Minister, she made highly objectionable and disrespectful remarks against the Calcutta High Court and its judges. Today, although the people of West Bengal have removed her from the post of Chief Minister and she is no longer even an MLA, she remains unable to shed that mindset," Khan told reporters.He further alleged that Banerjee had considered herself above the rule of law in the state."She used to consider herself above the rule of law in West Bengal, and that attitude persists. Article Title: Nepal floods revive Bihar’s annual nightmare: Why the state faces flooding every year
Article Text:
The rivers that sustain the region for most of the year turn dangerous during the monsoon

What was the trigger this time?

Why does Bihar drown every year?

Class I refers to flash floods, which occur due to rainfall in Nepal, have a short lead time of around eight hours between forecast and flood, and recede quickly.

Class II refers to river floods, with a lead time of 24 hours and floodwaters that take a week or more to recede.

Class III refers to drainage congestion at river confluences, where the lead time exceeds 24 hours and the water lasts the entire monsoon season, receding only after about three months.

Class IV refers to permanently waterlogged areas.

Embankments: Solution or part of the problem?

Everybody loves a good flood

The traditions around floods

NEW DELHI: Boats replacing cars on flooded roads, families moving to relief camps and swollen rivers spilling into villages. North Bihar is bracing for familiar scenes once again as floodwaters from Nepal move downstream.Floods have long been a part of life in northern Bihar. But a growing population and rapid urbanisation have made their impact more severe over the years.The rivers that sustain the region for most of the year turn dangerous during the monsoon. And for people living here, there is little choice but to face the floods, rebuild and prepare for the cycle to repeat itself.Bihar minister Ramkripal Yadav said the state government is closely monitoring the flood threat in Bihar in view of the tragedy in Nepal."Bihar is adjacent to Nepal, and the water that has come from Nepal in the past has affected many areas of Bihar, leading to loss of life and property, destruction of crops and homes. The Bihar government and the chief minister himself are monitoring this," Yadav told ANI.He assured that the state government will extend every possible help to those affected."The Bihar government will provide every possible help. The flood victims of Bihar have the first right on Bihar's treasury, and it is secure for them.The government will work," he added.A glacial collapse at the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26 triggered a flash flood in Nepal that has claimed more than 600 lives.Analysis of satellite imagery indicated that a large mass of ice and rock may have fallen into the Lende Khola river, temporarily blocking its flow and creating a natural dam that later breached, sending floodwaters downstream.Due to the collapse, a large volume of ice and rock debris entered the Lende Khola, a tributary of the Bhote Koshi river in Nepal, generating a sudden surge that carried water, sediment and large boulders downstream.The scale of the devastation can be gauged from the fact that twelve hydropower plants were reportedly knocked offline, dozens of bridges were swept away and the only road connecting the valley to the rest of Nepal was destroyed.Nature could not care less about political borders. And a flood that originated in Nepal will not stop at the border. From Nepal, the floodwaters will eventually move into north Bihar, before flowing into West Bengal and eventually Bangladesh, where they will empty into the sea.Speaking to The Times of India, IIT-trained civil engineer and flood expert Dinesh Mishra said Bihar's locational disadvantage is one of the reasons why it drowns every year in floods. He said the state is situated in such a way that water comes directly through the south-flowing rivers from Nepal."The first reason is Bihar's locational disadvantage. Bihar is situated in such a way that water comes directly from the mountains," Mishra said."All the rivers that enter Bihar from Nepal are south-flowing. So, the area north of the Ganga will inevitably remain waterlogged. And if it does not, there will be drought in the region," he added.Rivers originating from the Himalayas, like Kosi, Gandak, Burhi Gandak and Bagmati, carry huge volumes of silt with them to Bihar. When the water level increases due to rain, these rivers overflow their banks.This makes Bihar India's most flood-prone state, with 76 per cent of the population in north Bihar living under the threat of floods.Bihar's disaster management authority classifies floods into four categories.This year, according to Bihar water resources department, the Gandak river has crossed the danger mark in Gopalganj, while the barrage at Valmikinagar released around 99,800 cusecs of water at 8 pm on Saturday."The water level of several rivers, including the Gandak, Kosi, Burhi Gandak and the Ganga, has been rising. Incessant rainfall in the catchment areas of Nepal has led to rivers touching or flowing above the danger level at several places," a senior official of the water resources department said.People in West Champaran, East Champaran, Sitamarhi and Muzaffarpur, besides Gopalganj, Saran and Vaishali, have also been facing heightened fears over the past three days following an unprecedented inflow of water from Nepal.Other than flooding, another concern is soil erosion along the banks of swollen rivers.For over a century, embankments along rivers have been a major preventive measure against floods. Successive governments built these walls along river banks to prevent rivers from deviating from their course and protect settlements.However, Dinesh Mishra said these embankments are the root cause of the havoc wreaked by floods rather than being the solution."You build embankments basically to prevent river water from spilling out. But if floodwater that would naturally flow into the river is stopped, the water has nowhere to go," Mishra said."If it cannot return to the river, it will move into areas that were previously not affected by floods," he added.Mishra said Kosi once had space to spread and deposit its sediments, but embankments have now confined the river. With the sediments having nowhere to go, the riverbed has been rising, making the Kosi increasingly prone to overflowing."The river carries silt with it, and because of the embankments, the riverbed continues to rise," he said.Interestingly, Flood Atlas of Bihar, prepared by Isro along with the central and state governments, also says that "there must be a realisation that minimising the risk and damage from floods may be a more rational way of flood management rather than formulating structural measures along the dynamic rivers such as the Kosi."During the conversation, Mishra, however, rejected the notion that floods have always been a source of sorrow for Bihar. He said floods are also a time of celebration.He said farmers eagerly wait for floods because, as he put it, "a fresh layer of silt is deposited on the fields after floods, making the soil more fertile."He added that in the remote villages of north Bihar, people sometimes wait for floods because relief funds and the attention of politicians are also drawn towards villages where little development work has been done."People have been made this way. Earlier, they had clear SOPs to protect themselves during floods. But now, because they have become dependent on the government for relief, lives are lost," he said.For generations, floods in north Bihar were not simply seen as a force to be feared. They were woven into the rhythm of life, with people learning to live alongside the rivers rather than trying to keep them at bay."Our ancestors knew this was a water-rich, flood-prone region. When they settled here, they must have done so with that understanding," Mishra said.The relationship with the rivers was deeply personal. People revered them as mothers, and when the rains failed, women in villages would perform rituals to invoke the rivers and call for water.But when the floodwaters refused to recede, another ritual would follow. Women would gather with fruits, flowers, sandalwood, akshat and sindoor to persuade the river to leave.The rivers were considered unmarried, Mishra said, and women would even "threaten" them with marriage if they refused to listen.These traditions show how closely floods have been tied to life in north Bihar for generations.People did not always see the rivers only as a threat. They depended on them for water, fertile soil and agriculture, even as they feared the destruction that came when the rivers overflowed.That relationship continues even today. Every monsoon, the same rivers bring both relief and anxiety. And once the water recedes, people clean their homes, return to their fields and begin rebuilding knowing that the floods may return the next year.
Article Summary: A glacial collapse at the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26 triggered a flash flood in Nepal that has claimed more than 600 lives. Bihar minister Ramkripal Yadav said the state government is closely monitoring the flood threat in Bihar in view of the tragedy in Nepal.

Article Title: ‘No question of bringing back Article 370’: BJP hits out at Mirwaiz Umar Farooq

NEW DELHI: BJP Jammu and Kashmir spokesperson Altaf Thakur on Sunday rejected Kashmir's chief cleric chairman Mirwaiz Umar Farooq 's call for political parties to unite for the restoration of Article 370 , saying there was "no question" of bringing back the constitutional provision.Thakur said Parliament had taken a "historic" constitutional decision to abrogate Article 370 and that the Supreme Court had subsequently upheld it. He accused the Mirwaiz of making statements that could disturb the peace that has returned to the Valley after years of violence."Mirwaiz Umar Farooq needs to realize that Article 370 will not be reinstated. No political party, leader, or pressure group can undo the fundamental truth that Parliament has permanently buried Article 370," Thakur said.He said attempts to revive the issue risked pushing Kashmir back into a period of political instability."These kinds of statements are intended to incite people and disturb the tranquility of the Valley once more. This will never be permitted. The return of peace to Kashmir has come at a very high cost to the country. Thakur stated, "We cannot allow politically motivated statements to undermine or challenge the sacrifices made by our courageous security forces and civilians, including political workers who gave their lives for peace and democracy.Thakur said people in Kashmir should not be pushed into another cycle of violence, shutdowns and unrest after having endured years of disruption."Those who try to resurrect old fault lines need to realize that Kashmir has progressed. Our young people are looking for the chances to educate themselves, work, entrepreneurship, investment, and travel. "They don't want to go back to a time, when violence dictated the future and shutdown calendars controlled their lives," he added in the statement.Thakur said political parties were free to express their views within the Constitution, but argued that repeatedly seeking reversal of a constitutional decision upheld by the Supreme Court was futile."Democracy gives the right to speak and participate, but democracy cannot be reduced to repeatedly demanding the reversal of a constitutional decision that has already been upheld by the highest court of the country," he stated.He also reiterated the BJP's position that statehood for Jammu and Kashmir would be restored at an appropriate time, while insisting that statehood and Article 370 were separate issues."Statehood and Article 370 are clearly different. The government has declared that statehood would be restored at a suitable moment. However, there is no way that Article 370 could be reinstated,". "Those who are causing confusion on this matter need are advised to stop misleading the public," he stated.Earlier, Mirwaiz had criticised the National Conference government's performance, saying its current position differed from commitments made during the 2024 Assembly elections."The people's rights have been taken away, Jammu & Kashmir has been split, and all of our legal and constitutional obligations have been totally disregarded," he said.While acknowledging that issues such as electricity, roads and development were important, Mirwaiz said they were secondary to what he described as the broader question concerning the status of Jammu and Kashmir.“ But I think these are secondary issues. The real issue is that the very existence of the people of Jammu & Kashmir is under threat. At this juncture, all political parties in J&K should not only raise their voice for the restoration of statehood but also seek the restoration of Article 370, which was the basis accession (with India),” he stated.Mirwaiz also alleged that the Union government had broken its commitments to the people of Jammu and Kashmir dating back to 1947, including constitutional guarantees.
Article Summary: Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, chief cleric of Kashmir, criticized by the BJP's Jammu and Kashmir unit. Thakur said attempts to revive the issue risked pushing Kashmir back into a period of political instability. He accused the Mirwaiz of making statements that could disturb the peace that has returned to the Valley.

Article Title: PM Modi received by Uzbek President Mirziyoyev in Tashkent, leaders share car ride

PM Narendra Modi with Uzbekistan Shavkat President Mirziyoyev

PM Modi's 'car' diplomacy

Prime Minister Narendra Modi received a warm and personal welcome from Uzbekistan President Shavkat Mirziyoyev after arriving in capital Tashkent on Saturday for a two-day state visit.From the airport, the two leaders travelled together by car to the presidential palace, marking the latest instance of PM Modi sharing a car ride with a world leader. They held a dinner meeting at the presidential palace.During the visit, the first leg of the prime minister’s two-nation tour, PM Modi will hold delegation-level talks with the Uzbek president to further strengthen the strategic partnership between the two countries.The discussions will cover cooperation in trade and investment, defence, digital connectivity, energy, education and people-to-people ties, while also setting the agenda for future bilateral engagement.In his departure statement, PM Modi noted that the India-Uzbekistan Strategic Partnership had witnessed “significant advancement” in recent years.“I look forward to my discussions with President Mirziyoyev on further deepening our cooperation in trade and investment, digital connectivity, defence, energy, and on advancing our shared visions of Viksit Bharat and Yangi Uzbekistan,” he wrote on X.The visit marks his fourth trip to Uzbekistan since taking office.He previously visited the country in 2015, 2016 and 2022.From Tashkent, PM Modi will travel to Bishkek at the invitation of Kyrgyz President Sadyr Zhaparov to attend the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit, which will mark 25 years of the organisation.PM Modi first “carpooled” with a world leader during his 2014 visit to the United States, when he shared a car ride with then-US President Barack Obama.However, since last year, car rides with world leaders have become a recurring feature of what has been described as the prime minister's "informal diplomacy."In September last year, during his visit to China for the SCO Summit, PM Modi travelled in the same car as Vladimir Putin, reciprocating the gesture months later when the Russian president visited New Delhi in December.Since then, he has shared car rides with world leaders including French President Emmanuel Macron, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi arrived in capital Tashkent on Saturday for a two-day state visit. Article Title: 'Took off for Kathmandu blissfully unaware': Shashi Tharoor on deadly Nepal floods
Article Text:
Tharoor said he was “blissfully unaware” of the devastation caused by a sudden flash flood in Nepal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Thursday said that he was “blissfully unaware” of the devastation caused by a sudden flash flood in Nepal’s Rasuwa district when he left for Kathmandu on Wednesday."A severe, sudden flash flood struck northern Nepal’s Rasuwa district near the Tibet border, causing widespread destruction along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers. Global warming and/or an earthquake in Tibet may have caused a large chunk of a glacier to break off and fall into the valley below, experts surmise," Tharoor said in a post on X.Tharoor added that the flooding had destroyed at least 19 motorable bridges and washed away around 40 km of the Betrawati–Rasuwagadhi highway. Eight operational hydropower projects were also reported to have sustained heavy damage.Tharoor said he supported the Indian government’s immediate pledge of relief assistance to Nepal, adding that the country would need substantial help in responding to the destruction.He also expressed concern over the loss of life and those still missing, including Indians affected by the disaster."I fully support the Indian government’s immediate pledge of relief assistance.Nepal needs all the help it can get. My heart goes out to the victims and their loved ones, who include large numbers of Indian tourists, including a hundred performing the Kailash-Mansarovar Yatra. Prayers for the missing; may they be rescued soon," Tharoor said.The disaster has left at least 270 people dead and 826 missing in Nepal, while three people have died and 558 remain unaccounted for in Tibet, according to authorities.The scale of destruction has hampered rescue operations, with Nepalese officials reporting that dozens of bridges were destroyed and nearly 40 kilometres (25 miles) of roads damaged.The Nepalese Army launched helicopter operations on Thursday morning, rescuing more than 100 people from flood-affected areas, army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet said. At least eight foreign nationals were also airlifted to Kathmandu, while army teams evacuated people trapped inside facilities associated with the Trishuli hydropower project.India is also coordinating efforts to assist its nationals stranded in the affected areas. Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said five major groups, comprising around 288 Indian nationals, had been identified.“ The first group of 73 people who are working on the Trishuli-1 power project. Then, two separate groups of 37 and 49 nationals from Tamil Nadu, who traveled for Kailash Mansarovar Yatra through Samrat and Fly Everest Travels. There is a group of 32 Indian nationals from West Bengal who traveled with the help of Samrat Travels in Timure, which is in Rasuwa district.”“Then, a group of 61 Indian nationals from different states and then a group of 33 Indian nationals from Kerala. These are five major groups who comprise, by and large, 288 people that we are talking about,” he added.Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah and offered India’s assistance for rescue and relief operations.“India is prepared to provide Nepal with all possible types of humanitarian assistance,” PM Modi said, adding that Indian teams were coordinating rescue and relief efforts.The United Nations is also supporting the response, with agencies deploying personnel to assist local authorities. UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric warned of a “massive humanitarian need” as rescue and relief operations continued.The disaster has also renewed concerns over the Himalayan region’s exposure to extreme weather events and glacial hazards, particularly in areas where difficult terrain and damaged infrastructure can complicate emergency response.
Article Summary: A severe, sudden flash flood struck northern Nepal’s Rasuwa district near the Tibet border, causing widespread destruction along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers. The disaster has left at least 270 people dead and 826 missing in Nepal, while three people have died and 558 remain unaccounted for in Tibet. India is also coordinating efforts to assist its nationals stranded in the affected areas.

JAMMU: Security forces launched a joint search operation in the remote, hilly hamlet of Sumb in J&K’s Samba district after receiving information that a wireless set had been briefly activated in the area and satellite communication was detected around 1pm Tuesday.“The reported activation of Iridium satellite sets raised suspicion among security agencies, following which a combined team of the Army, police, and personnel from other forces rushed to Sumb’s Makoli village and initiated extensive searches in and around the area,” an official said Wednesday.“Terrorists often switch off such communication devices after contacting their handlers across the border,” said a source, adding that Iridium sets can be used on smartphones through the “Iridium GO!” mobile application, which creates a local Wi-Fi network that an iOS or Android phone can connect to.The operation continued until late Tuesday, but no satellite set or other suspicious material was found. NEW DELHI: Responding to letters written by SC judge Sandeep Mehta complaining against Rajasthan high court acting chief justice (ACJ) Sanjeev Prakash Sharma and seeking his transfer outside the state, CJI Surya Kant Wednesday said he has sought the ACJ’s response.Justice Mehta wrote three letters in as many weeks pleading for the transfer of Justice Sharma, who is retiring Sept 26, and appointment of a regular chief justice. Justice Mehta also complained as to why CJI Kant had not acted on his fervent pleas.Justice Mehta, who also hails from Rajasthan HC, has accused Justice Sharma of lacking in leadership qualities and alleged there was maladministration and malpractice on both judicial and administrative sides of HC.CJI Kant told TOI that the matter can be resolved only as per the established mechanism. “The Supreme Court cannot allow individual complaints concerning judges to be determined through competing claims in the media,” he said. He also released a public statement Wednesday decrying the attempt to hold a public trial over allegations made by one judge against another.Contents of the letters cannot be adjudicated in public domain and that judge concerned must be given a fair opportunity to place his response before any conclusion is reached.The fact that allegations have been made, therefore, cannot by itself be treated as a finding against the judge,” CJI Surya Kant’s statement said.The established mechanism for inquiring into allegations of an Supreme Court or High Court judge is the constitution of an in-house committee — comprising judges — by the Chief Justice of India, if he finds the response of the judge accused of misdemeanour or corrupt practices unsatisfactory and feels the charges are serious enough to warrant a deeper probe.CJI Kant, who is on a three-day official visit to Germany, also told TOI that he has already sought a response from Justice Sharma following the letters from Justice Mehta, who has alleged that there is “clear evidence of favouritism” by Justice Sharma. Justice Mehta’s complaints are being examined, CJI Surya Kant said.

Article Title: Two Malayali women killed in California; friend detained
Article Text:
Two Malayali women were killed in California, United States, allegedly by a friend.





THRISSUR/THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: Two Malayali women were killed in California, United States, allegedly by another Malayali woman who was their friend and lived in the same apartment complex, according to their relatives. An investigation is underway.One of the victims was identified as 35-year-old Anjana from Mudikkode near Mannuthy in Thrissur. The other was Ann Mary Mathew (40) of Kesavadasapuram, Thiruvananthapuram . The victims’ families have alleged that both Anjana and Ann Mary were killed by their friend Anila. According to information received by the families, San Jose police have taken the suspect into custody and are investigating the case.Jerry Sam Joseph, a neighbour and family friend, said Ann Mary’s family had received information that she had an issue with the suspect over a job-related matter. However, Anjana’s cousin Vinod said the family had not yet received any information about the motive behind the killings.The suspect allegedly entered Ann Mary’s house and stabbed her, Jerry said.According to information received by Anjana’s relatives, Anjana was killed after Anila allegedly knocked her down with a car.The killings reportedly took place around noon on Friday (US time). Anjana’s family in Keralam was informed about the incident on Saturday (Indian time).Ann Mary had been living in the US for around 10 years and was working as an engineer, according to her neighbours. She was married to Pallathra Jacob, a native of Chingavanam in Kottayam, who is also in the US.Anjana had been working as a teacher in California for nearly six years, according to her relatives. Her husband, Vijeesh, who hails from Vilangannoor near Peechi, is also employed there. Vijayan Vilangannur, Anjana’s father-in-law, said his son Vijeesh was extremely distressed by the incident and was unable to speak to him.Thrissur collector Sikha Surendran said she had asked Anjana’s family to submit details of the incident so that they could be forwarded to the NORKA secretary, who would then approach Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) for assistance in bringing the body back to the state. Meanwhile, Ann Mary’s relatives said they were awaiting further information from US and that arrangements were being made to bring her body back to Thiruvananthapuram.
Article Summary: One of the victims was identified as 35-year-old Anjana from Mudikkode near Mannuthy in Thrissur. The other was Ann Mary Mathew (40) of Kesavadasapuram, Thiruvananthapurams. The victims’ families have alleged that both AnJana and Ann Mary were killed by their friend Anila. San Jose police have taken the suspect into custody and are investigating.

Article Title: US strikes Iran's Larak Island after weeks of calm; Tehran retaliates by hitting US bases in Jordan
Article Text:
US strike marked first strike in months on Iran

US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers near Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz late Sunday, in their first confirmed military action against Iran in a month, breaking a weeks-long lull in fighting. Iran quickly vowed retaliation, with state television later showing what it said were ballistic missiles fired at US bases in Jordan.Jordanian forces said they intercepted eight missiles that entered the country’s airspace early Monday. Meanwhile Iran international also reported that explosions were heard at US bases on Qatar. These attacks have not been confirmed by US officials.The US Central Command alleged Iran's Revolutionary Guard forces had been preparing to launch rockets carrying sea mines into the Strait of Hormuz when they were targeted. Tim Hawkins, a Centcom spokesperson, said the US military had observed the preparations, reported AP. The US had completed clearing sea mines from international shipping routes in the strait the previous week.Iranian semiofficial media, quoted by AP reported the explosions near Larak Island, while the Revolutionary Guard acknowledged that several of its fighters and civilians had been killed or wounded.The head of the national security commission of the Iranian parliament Ebrahim Azizi condemened the attack saying on X (translated from Farsi), "Retesting our will only makes the cost of your humiliating defeats even heavier. Undoubtedly, no crime, at any level, goes unanswered; a response that is devastating, more painful, and instructive, which will complete the chain of your failures. Wait in fear and terror!"He then made another statement in English adding, "Test our will once more, and pay a heavier price. Retaliation is coming; JUST RUN!"The strike marked the first confirmed US attack on Iran since July 29, when Washington said it had launched a “heavy wave of strikes” against dozens of Revolutionary Guard targets, including coastal surveillance and defence sites.President Donald Trump later said on August 1 that he would hold off on further strikes following appeals from Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE.The latest military action came days after the Trump administration said it would prioritise economic pressure over further strikes in an effort to force Tehran to end the war. The strategy involved threatening sanctions against countries and entities that continue doing business with Iran.Revolutionary Guard spokesperson Gen. Hossein Mohebi called Sunday’s attack a “fatal mistake” and warned that Washington would face military and economic consequences.The administration’s reliance on sanctions also comes as US officials weigh depleted munitions stockpiles after more than six months of conflict, raising concerns about the impact on American military readiness elsewhere.Trump has increasingly played down the prospect of a quick end to the war, saying last week that he was “not in a hurry” to bring Iran back to negotiations. He has continued to argue that Iran’s leadership and military capabilities have been severely weakened.Iranian officials, however, have maintained a defiant stance. Recent appointments to senior security positions have signalled Tehran’s intent to continue resisting pressure despite years of sanctions and internal repression.Trump has repeatedly said the US-Israel campaign has devastated Iran’s navy and air force. Tehran estimates that the conflict has caused about $270 billion in direct and indirect damage, while Israeli strikes in the opening weeks severely weakened Iran’s political leadership.Despite those losses, Iran retains significant leverage through the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial global energy route. Tehran has targeted vessels in and around the waterway, where commercial traffic has fallen sharply since the war began.The strait normally carries about 20% of the world’s oil, but relatively few tankers carrying crude and liquefied natural gas are now willing to risk the route. Iran still possesses enough drones and missiles to threaten vessels passing through the waterway.Oil prices rose after Sunday’s US strike, with US crude gaining 1.8% to $84.94 a barrel and Brent crude rising 1.9% to $89.79.Iran has also maintained that the US cannot use the Strait of Hormuz until Washington fulfils its obligations under a memorandum of understanding signed with Tehran in June, even after Iran and Oman agree on a management arrangement for the waterway.Trump has repeatedly said the strait is “open”, pointing to 24 vessels that crossed it last week. That remains far below the roughly 130 vessels that passed through each day before the war.A US Navy-overseen multinational coalition said commercial traffic remained at “reduced levels” on Sunday. Separately, the UK Maritime Trade Organization said an unidentified projectile struck a tanker north of Khasab, Oman, on Saturday. No casualties or environmental damage were reported, and there was no immediate claim of responsibility.The US military said it had redirected 83 commercial vessels and disabled three others as part of its blockade of Iranian ports.
Article Summary: US Central Command alleged Iran's Revolutionary Guard forces had been preparing to launch rockets carrying sea mines into the Strait of Hormuz. Iran quickly vowed retaliation, with state television later showing what it said were ballistic missiles fired at US bases in Jordan. The strike marked the first confirmed US attack on Iran since July 29.

Article Title: 16-year-old UP girl gang-raped inside moving bus during 47-km ride to Delhi's Kashmere Gate
Article Text:
A 16-year-old student was allegedly gang-raped inside a moving sleeper bus.





NEW DELHI: A 16-year-old Class 11 student from Uttar Pradesh was allegedly gang-raped inside a moving sleeper bus after she boarded the vehicle seeking help while stranded in heavy rain, police said.The incident took place on the night of August 4 after the teenager, from Mainpuri district, left home following a disagreement with her family and set out to meet her cousin in Noida.According to police, the girl got off at Pari Chowk by mistake amid heavy rain and darkness. An empty sleeper bus passing through the area then stopped after she signalled for help.The driver, Kuldeep, and conductor, Sandeep, allegedly told her that the bus was headed towards Noida Sector 63 and allowed her to board.Police said the conductor allegedly began making obscene advances towards the teenager soon after the bus started moving. The girl has alleged that both the driver and conductor subsequently raped her and threatened to kill her when she resisted.The bus then travelled nearly 47 kilometres towards Kashmere Gate. The accused allegedly abandoned the teenager on Ring Road near the Kashmere Gate bus terminal late at night and fled.The terrified student approached Kashmere Gate police and reported the incident.Police subsequently arrested Kuldeep and Sandeep from a bus parking area in Timarpur and seized the sleeper bus. The vehicle has been sent for forensic examination.Investigators said the bus had earlier broken down and was taken to a workshop in Surajpur for repairs. After the repairs were completed, the driver and conductor were taking the empty bus to Timarpur when they encountered the teenager at Pari Chowk.Police said the sleeper bus had curtains around its berths, which allegedly helped the accused conceal what was happening inside during the journey.The bus covered around 47 kilometres between Pari Chowk and Kashmere Gate before the teenager was allegedly abandoned.Further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: The incident took place on the night of August 4 after the teenager, from Mainpuri district, left home following a disagreement with her family. The girl got off at Pari Chowk by mistake amid heavy rain and darkness. An empty sleeper bus passing through the area then stopped after she signalled for help. Police said the conductor allegedly began making obscene advances towards the teenager soon after the bus started moving.

Article Title: Nepal floods: Boy waves T-shirt for help, climbs onto helicopter in dramatic rescue
Article Text:
A young boy trapped on the roof of a house surrounded by raging floodwaters was rescued by the Nepal Army after he used his T-shirt to signal a passing helicopter.

A young boy trapped on the roof of a house surrounded by raging floodwaters was rescued by the Nepal Army after he used his T-shirt to signal a passing helicopter.A video of the dramatic rescue showed the child standing on the rooftop and repeatedly waving his T-shirt as a Nepal Army helicopter approached the area.With floodwaters cutting off the house, the boy appeared to have no other way to draw the rescuers' attention. He continued waving until the helicopter hovered over the building.As the helicopter moved closer, the boy reached for its landing skid before grabbing the hand of an army officer seated inside. With the soldier's assistance, he pulled himself up and climbed aboard the helicopter.People watching the operation could be heard applauding and cheering as the child was safely rescued.The rescue came as Nepal continued a massive operation following devastating flash floods and landslides that have killed hundreds of people and left thousands missing.Rescue efforts have increasingly focused on people believed to be trapped inside tunnels at hydropower projects damaged by the floods.Around 10,000 Nepali troops have been deployed for tunnel rescue operations, alongside specialists from China and India, according to Dharam Raj Uprety, chief of Nepal's national disaster management authority.The disaster struck after torrents of ice, rock, mud and debris swept through mountain valleys and rivers on Wednesday, causing widespread destruction along the Nepal-China border.Nepal's disaster authorities said 781 people had died and 2,502 remained missing. More than 90,000 people are believed to have been affected by the disaster.Rescue operations remain underway as authorities work to locate missing people and evacuate those stranded in flood-hit areas.
Article Summary: A video of the dramatic rescue showed the child standing on the rooftop and repeatedly waving his T-shirt as a Nepal Army helicopter approached the area. The rescue came as Nepal continued a massive operation following devastating flash floods and landslides that have killed hundreds of people and left thousands missing.

Article Title: Did US military warn Hegseth over Iran war strain before latest escalation? What report claims
Article Text:
US military leaders reportedly warned Iran that operation has become “too much for too long”, citing strain on troops and readiness.

Navy under mounting strain

Latest escalation came despite warnings?

Several senior US military leaders reportedly warned Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth that prolonging large-scale operations against Iran was unsustainable and could weaken the military’s ability to respond to threats elsewhere, including against the US homeland.The assessment was prepared for Hegseth and recorded in the August 14 edition of the Secretary of Defense Orders Book (SDOB), weeks before the latest escalation in fighting between the United States and Iran, according to The Wall Street Journal citing sources. It reflected concerns over the continued deployment of US forces to the Middle East as the Iran conflict entered its sixth month.The heads of the Army, Navy and Air Force, along with the four-star commanders overseeing US operations in Europe, Asia and Latin America, raised concerns over the strain the prolonged operation was placing on troops, equipment and military readiness, the people said.The SDOB, typically produced twice a month, tracks the worldwide availability of US warships, aircraft, personnel and weapons systems and helps inform Pentagon decisions on force deployments.At the time of the assessment, US Central Command had more than 50,000 troops on alert in the region as President Donald Trump continued to demand that Tehran reopen the Strait of Hormuz and accept US terms for ending the conflict.Trump had also kept open the possibility of further military action.The August 14 orders book directed some forces in the Middle East to remain deployed through September and others into 2027. That prospect prompted several senior commanders to formally object to extending their forces, while saying they would carry out the orders.The commanders of US European Command, US Pacific Command and US Southern Command, along with the Navy's top admiral, issued what the document described as a “non-concur”; indicating disagreement with the deployment extensions but an intention to execute them.The military leaders warned that the Iran operation was drawing ships, aircraft and other equipment away from other theatres, limiting their ability to conduct missions and maintain training.Army and Air Force leadership agreed with extending their deployments but warned that doing so carried significant risks.Overall, the assessment described the Iran operation as “too much for too long,” according to one person familiar with it, as quoted by WSJ.The Navy has borne a particularly heavy burden, supplying dozens of vessels for the Iran campaign, including for combat operations, defence against Iranian attacks and the enforcement of Trump's blockade of Iranian ports.Some ship and crew deployments had already been extended by months.Adm. Daryl Caudle, the chief of Naval Operations, told Hegseth that the Navy could not sustain its current level of support for the Iran conflict because there was no anticipated end date, according to people familiar with the assessment.Caudle also indicated that barely one-fourth of the Navy's destroyer fleet was ready to deploy, a sharp decline from prewar levels. Continued demands from the Iran operation were also jeopardising ship maintenance and the fleet's availability for other potential conflicts.At a recent event in Norfolk, Caudle described the deployment extensions as “very challenging for our sailors.”“I typically am not a big fan of extensions, and I push back hard on that, but the enemy gets a vote,” he said, according to a Navy transcript.The strain was also being felt by other branches of the military.The commanders of European and Southern commands warned that providing ships and surveillance aircraft to Central Command had degraded their ability to fulfil homeland-defence responsibilities.Adm Samuel Paparo, head of Pacific Command, objected to the level of support his command was continually required to provide, including an aircraft carrier strike group and destroyers.The Army was also preparing to extend deployments. Elements of the 82nd Airborne Division, which mobilised 2,000 soldiers in March in response to the Iran war, were set for deployments lasting up to a year. Those troops would be central to any potential ground invasion of Iran.Units operating Patriot air-defence systems were also expected to have their deployments extended.The prolonged war has meanwhile depleted key U.S. military stocks. The Pentagon has faced shortages of Patriot and Terminal High Altitude Area Defense interceptors, as well as long-range Tomahawk missiles. About 25% of the Pentagon's Reaper drone fleet had also been lost, while U.S. bases in the Middle East had suffered billions of dollars in damage, according to earlier reports.The Trump administration has rejected reports that the U.S. is facing significant munitions shortages.The concerns in the August 14 assessment predated the latest escalation in the US-Iran conflict, which means the most recent US strikes on Larak Island late Sunday and promopting Iran's retaliation.The assessment nevertheless highlights the military readiness dilemma facing the Trump administration: sustaining a prolonged campaign against Iran could leave fewer forces and weapons available to respond to other threats, particularly in Europe and the Indo-Pacific.A Pentagon spokesman said decisions on the scope and duration of deployments are based on the current threat assessment, presidential priorities and advice from senior military commanders.The Pentagon declined to discuss the SDOB or specific “concurrences, non-concurrences, or risk assessments” provided during force-allocation deliberations.
Article Summary: US military leaders reportedly warned Iran that operation has become ‘too much for too long’, citing strain on troops and readiness.Latest escalation came despite warnings? According to sources, the assessment predated the latest escalation in fighting between the United States and Iran.

Article Title: Watch: Grand Canyon flash flood sends bunkhouse, boulders rushing downstream; at least 20 missing
Article Text:
The iconic national park has issued alerts as at least 20 people are missing

A powerful flash flood tore through Arizona’s Grand Canyon, sending torrents of muddy water, boulders and debris through Bright Angel Canyon and into the Colorado River. The National Park Service (NPS) said at least 20 people may be missing or unaccounted for, prompting a public appeal for information.The flooding happened on August 29, but the park reported aftermath on Sunday (local time) about the damage and the missing people.Meanwhile, more than 60 people were evacuated from Phantom Ranch and Bright Angel Campground as the flood swept through the canyon. Footbridges were destroyed, the creek bed was dramatically reshaped and debris, including what appeared to be a bunkhouse, was carried downstream while campers seeked safety.The NPS is asking for information about hikers and backpackers who were in the Bright Angel Creek corridor on August 29, including people who had reservations at affected campgrounds. Phantom Ranch, Bright Angel Campground and the North Kaibab Trail remain closed.The flood also damaged the Grand Canyon’s sole water pipeline, forcing the park to suspend overnight hotel stays from August 31 and ask residents to conserve water. The pipeline is already being rehabilitated as part of a $208 million infrastructure project.The flooding followed roughly 0.5 to 1 inch of rain in about 30 minutes, with much of the water running off immediately through the steep terrain. More rain and thunderstorms are possible, raising the threat of further flooding.

More than 60 people were evacuated from Phantom Ranch and Bright Angel Campground as the flood swept through the canyon.
